value.body: Diabetes educators help people with diabetes and their families understand the condition and manage it day to day: what to eat, how to check blood sugar, how to take insulin and when to seek help. They work in hospitals, diabetes clinics, endocrinology practices, pharma patient-support programmes and digital health services.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc in Nutrition & Dietetics, nursing, or allied health

items.label: Common add-on
items.value: A certificate course in diabetes education
items.note: Offered by professional bodies and hospitals

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Glucometers, CGM reports, patient education material

items.label: People with diabetes in India
items.note: Survey-based estimate across 31 states and UTs

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many start as dietitians or nutritionists in hospital diabetes clinics and add a diabetes educator certificate. Pharma patient-support programmes and digital health services also hire nutrition graduates as diabetes counsellors.

value.title: At a glance
items: The role works alongside doctors; it does not prescribe medicines.
Common next steps: senior educator, clinical dietitian, or programme lead in patient support.
Language skills and patience with patients matter a lot.

competition.note: B.Sc (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
